study type: Case-control study with in vitro experimental validation
outcome: Protein transcription and expression levels of GPRC6A/PI3K/AKT/MMP2/MMP9
cohort: The study participants were 15 pregnant women, including 10 diagnosed with Placental Accreta Spectrum (PAS) and 5 with normal pregnancies, from whom placental tissues were collected.
finding: Placental L-Arginine concentrations were significantly higher in PAS patients, and in vitro, L-Arginine promoted trophoblast proliferation and migration by upregulating the GPRC6A/PI3K/AKT pathway.
cross-section timing: Placental tissues were collected from pregnant women, likely at the time of delivery or clinical intervention.
